task: Make the default 10-file cap for File-based Datasources configurable while retaining 10 by default and supporting higher limits; upload and process large create/edit selections in performance-safe batches.

key_reasoning.reason: The change spans runtime customer configuration, the shared FilesDropzone selection UI, datasource form binding and Yup validation, and the create/update submission boundary. The same shared dropzone is used by both creation and editing, so configured capacity must consistently account for retained server files and newly selected files.

Product intent is clear: preserve 10 as the default, allow a client-configured higher maximum, and protect performance for large selections. Important details remain unresolved: the exact configuration ID and whether the configured maximum applies to an edit's combined retained-plus-new count, batch size, progress semantics, and retry/partial-failure behavior.

The existing index create and update APIs accept all raw File objects in one multipart request. Splitting a create request into batches can create multiple datasources or duplicate indexing work. Safe batching therefore depends on a backend contract such as staged uploads plus one final create/update, or an index upload-session/batch protocol with idempotency and cleanup rules.

Expected work touches approximately seven to ten production files: configuration key/accessor, FilesDropzone and FileDropArea, IndexTypeFile, form schema/binding, create-index hook, and datasource transport. Focused tests are also needed for configuration fallback, limits, schema parity, chunking/order, and failed-batch handling.

The UI can consume GET v1/config only after the customer configuration key/value is defined, and transport batching cannot be correctly implemented in this repository without backend API ownership confirming the transaction, idempotency, partial-failure, and processing contract. This dependency is material but belongs to the same product capability rather than a separate user story.

The feature crosses configuration/state, presentation and accessibility, client validation, form submission orchestration, and HTTP multipart transport. It also requires preserving current edit-only parameters such as uploaded_files, reindex options, CSV settings, project rename, embedding model, and guardrails.

red_flags_applied: Backend batching contract required before changing create/update transport; do not issue multiple index-create requests for one selection.
Partial batch failure needs defined retry, cleanup/rollback, and user-visible outcome semantics.
Configuration must safely fall back to 10 for missing, malformed, zero, or negative values and must align with backend limits.
